3CIT.why: Down about 64% from the ₹52 issue price (52-week range ₹13-25; down 29% over a year). Reported earlier issues: FY25 profit slipped to a loss of ₹0.06 crore, the CFO resigned in June 2025, the annual report was delayed and auditors flagged missing bank balance confirmations. The latest company-reported news is a turnaround: FY26 profit after tax of ₹57.5 lakh and revenue up to ₹58.5 crore from ₹36.5 crore (not verified against audited filings). Trading is very thin.
3CIT.outlook: No analyst rating or target found. It is setting up an AMD Centre of Excellence in Pune and a Digital Labs project in Manipur. Market cap is only about ₹11-15 crore.

SATTRIX.why: About 2.4x the ₹121 issue price (52-week range ₹226-451) but down about 21% in six months. No clear cause found. Filings show an all-share acquisition of Sattrix Software Solutions and a preferential issue of 45.5 lakh shares at ₹347 or more, which can dilute holders. Net profit is small (about ₹4 crore TTM against a market cap near ₹370-400 crore), receivables are 244 days and working-capital days doubled to 117.
SATTRIX.outlook: No broker research, targets or guidance found. P/E is 49-62 and ROE sources range from 4% to 18%. It sells cybersecurity services. Check the latest quarterly results and the preferential issue.

AKIKO.why: About 5.4x the ₹77 issue price and up about 107% in six months to a ₹438.95 high in September 2026. MarketsMojo ties the move to a Mojo grade upgrade to Buy on 13 July, record highs and strong volume, and fundamentals: ROE 21.3%, debt to equity 0.10, and annual sales and operating profit growth near 126% and 124%. Revenue was about ₹122.7 crore in FY26 against ₹63.6 crore. It earns commission selling credit cards (a DSA), which is a small, volatile model.
AKIKO.outlook: No analyst target or guidance found. P/E is about 19-23 but price to book is 6-7x. Market cap about ₹450 crore after a very rapid rise, so the price is volatile.

DTL.why: About 24% above the ₹100 issue price (52-week range ₹82-178). It is loss-making (TTM about -₹3 crore, ROE -20%, a quarterly loss of ₹3.88 crore on revenue of ₹52.3 crore, up 76%). A fundraise through equity or convertibles and a ₹4.58 crore warrant issue (April 2026) point to dilution risk. It is a technical staffing and recruitment business; trading is thin.
DTL.outlook: No broker targets, consensus or guidance found. Price-to-book is 4.4x while earnings are negative, so valuation is stretched. Check the EGM outcome and fundraise terms.

RNFI.why: About 3.1x the ₹105 issue price, up about 45% in six months to September 2026 but down 12% over a year (52-week range ₹216-388). No source named a catalyst. Fundamentals: TTM profit about ₹20 crore, ROE 25%, ROCE 33%. It provides domestic money transfer, IMPS, AEPS, recharges and tickets through a merchant network. P/E ranged 21-46 depending on the earnings base.
RNFI.outlook: No analyst targets or guidance found. Check the September-quarter results due on the exchanges.

SATECH.why: Down about 39% from the ₹59 issue price and from a post-listing peak of ₹250 (August 2024); down 36% over a year. Last half-year net income fell about 35% (₹2.9 crore against ₹4.5 crore). No source tied the fall to results. It is an IT consulting subsidiary of a foreign group.
SATECH.outlook: No analyst rating, guidance or 2026 forecast found. Market cap fell from about ₹59 crore to ₹47 crore over the summer.

PARAMATRIX.why: Down about 47% from the ₹110 issue price and 31% over a year (52-week range ₹51-96). No company-specific explanation was found. Institutional holdings are low (FIIs 2.1%) and daily volume can be as small as 8,400 shares. P/E estimates range from 14 to 55.
PARAMATRIX.outlook: No guidance or analyst view found. Simply Wall St scores valuation 2/6, future growth 0/6, past performance 3/6 and financial health 4/6. Market cap about ₹67 crore.

C2C.why: Down 22% from the ₹226 issue price, 73% over a year and 40% in six months (52-week range about ₹247-888); it fell 11% on 1 October 2026 to ₹185.90. No company-specific trigger was identified. FY26 revenue rose to ₹161.7 crore (₹117.5 crore) but profit fell to ₹18.3 crore from ₹28.8 crore, and management expects receivables of around 270 days. It was a defence-valuation darling that has cooled.
C2C.outlook: Management had guided to about ₹250 crore turnover for FY26, well above reported ₹161.7 crore; it expects steady free cash flow from around 2027, pending orders from the Navy and DRDO (details under NDA), a proposal pipeline of ₹1,144 crore and potential defence projects of about ₹2,700 crore. These are management claims and no analyst target exists.

CNINFOTECH.why: Down 71% from the ₹263 issue price and 61% in the year to December 2025 (52-week range ₹70-136). Profit is flat (₹25.8 crore in FY25 against ₹26.0 crore) with revenue up only to ₹105.7 crore; FII holding fell from 2.2% to 0.16% while promoters held about 75%. Sources report bearish technicals and no specific cause.
CNINFOTECH.outlook: No analyst target or guidance found. At about ₹83 the market cap is roughly ₹200 crore, so valuation is modest against flat profit. Check Q1 FY27 results.
